lyrics:
[Intro: muted funk guitar, four-on-the-floor kick, pulsing bass]

[Verse 1: dry male lead, close and flat]
Put away the glowing window
Put away the little light
You've been nodding at the table
You've been somewhere else all night
Hey, grown-ups, look up, we're right here

[Refrain: male lead, organ swells]
One more evening
One more thumb across a screen

[Verse 2: children's choir, rough and loud, same words]
Put away the glowing window
Put away the little light
You've been nodding at the table
You've been somewhere else all night
Hey, grown-ups, look up, we're right here

[Refrain: children's choir, organ swells]
One more evening
One more thumb across a screen

[Guitar Solo: long, bluesy, singing bends over the groove]

[Verse 3: male lead and children together]
We don't want another picture
We would rather have the day
There's a story you were telling
And you stopped it halfway
Hey, grown-ups, look up, we're right here

[Refrain: everyone, building]
One more evening
One more thumb across a screen

[Outro: groove continues, playground noise, a child calling]
Dad
Dad
Dad, watch this
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 104 BPM, 4/4, D minor. A steady, hypnotic disco pulse under a cold, accusing tune. Dry, dark and oddly danceable.

VOICE: A male lead with a dry, flat, slightly sneering delivery, close to the microphone. A choir of schoolchildren with unpolished voices and strong local accents sings the second verse and refrain loudly and a little out of tune, as children do. A single child speaks at the end.

INSTRUMENTS: A clean electric guitar playing tight, muted, funky chops. A four-on-the-floor kick drum with a crisp snare and steady hi-hat. A pulsing, repeating bass. A church-like organ swelling in the refrains. A lead electric guitar with a warm, singing tone for a long, blues-based solo. Playground sounds.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, the groove. 0:16 Verse 1, the man. 0:42 Refrain. 0:52 Verse 2, the children. 1:18 Refrain. 1:28 Guitar solo, sixteen bars or more. 2:20 Verse 3, the man and the children together. 2:46 Refrain, building. 3:00 Outro, the groove continues under playground noise and a child calling three times, fading by 3:45.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Late-1970s art rock with a disco rhythm section: very dry, tight and controlled, the children's choir roomy and raw by contrast.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The children's choir entering at 0:52.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: In 1979 the children sang against the teachers. Now they are singing to their own parents, and the last three words are a child trying to be seen. Anyone who grew up with the original is the target.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Accusation, recognition, a small plea.
